branches.source_phrase_ar: ملك الإنسان الشيء يملكه ملكا (maqayis)؛ الملك ما ملكت اليد من مال وخول (ayn;tahdhib)؛ ملكت الشيء أملكه ملكا (sihah)؛ وملكه المال والملك فهو مملك (sihah)؛ أملكت فلانة أمرها إذا جعل أمر طلاقها بيدها (tahdhib)؛ المملوك يختص في التعارف بالرقيق من الأملاك (mufradat)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, sahipliği bir şeyin elde veya hukuki denetimde bulunması ve üzerinde hükme bağlı tasarruf kurulması olarak birleştirir; devir, kölelik ve özel karar yetkisi bu ilişkinin tarihsel ya da kalıplaşmış uzantılarıdır.

branches.what_is_ar: ملك الشيء والمال وما ملكت اليد؛ جعل الشيء ملكا لغيره؛ المملوك والعبد وملك اليمين؛ حسن الملكة إلى المماليك؛ تفويض الأمر لصاحبه
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس مُلك السلطان العام ولا الإملاك للتزويج

concept_gloss.applicability: Yönetici kişiyi, halk üzerindeki hüküm gücünü ve bu gücün ülkesini birlikte temsil eder.

error_profile.preserves: Hükümdar, yönetim, halk, ülke ve egemenlik ilişkisini birlikte korur.

concept_map.definition: Bir hükümdarın halk üzerinde emir, yasak ve yönetim yetkisi kullanmasıyla kurulan kamusal hükümranlıktır. Bu alan hükümdarı, yönetim gücünü, hükmedilen ülkeyi ve ilahi bağlamda mutlak egemenliği kapsar.

facets.statement: Hükümdar, halk üzerinde emir ve yasak koyarak kamusal yönetim yetkisi kullanır.
Hükümranlık, yöneticinin halkı ve ülkesindeki etkili yönetim alanını kapsar.
İlahi bağlamda bütün varlık üzerindeki mutlak ve kalıcı egemenlik anlatılır.
Bir topluluk bir kişiyi başına geçirerek onu hükümdar konumuna getirir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Halk üzerinde yönetim ve siyaset yetkisi kullanan kişi kastedildiğinde uygundur.

error_profile.loses: Soyut hükümranlığı, ülkeyi ve ilahi mutlak egemenliği dışarıda bırakır.
error_profile.preserves: Kamusal yönetim yetkisini taşıyan katılımcıyı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Halk ve ülke üzerindeki yönetim gücü soyut olarak anlatıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Hükümdar kişisini ve birini hükümdar yapma eylemini açıkça göstermez.
error_profile.preserves: Kamusal egemenlik ve yönetim gücünü korur.

error_profile.adds: Belirli bir mal veya hak üzerinde özel aidiyet ekler.
error_profile.collision: Aynı kökün özel sahiplik dalıyla karışır.
error_profile.loses: Halk üzerinde emir, yasak ve siyaset yoluyla kurulan kamusal yönetimi kaybeder.
error_profile.preserves: Denetim ve yetki unsurunu sınırlı biçimde korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal, belirli bir malın kişisel sahipliğinden ve ilahi haberci varlığın adından ayrıdır.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, hükümdarı halk üzerinde emir ve yasak koyan yönetici olarak tanımlar; hükümranlık, ülke, halk üzerindeki siyaset ve özellikle ilahi mutlak egemenlik bu kamusal yönetim çekirdeğinde birleşir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Hükümdar ve hükümranlık çekirdeği korunur; ülke, mutlak ilahi egemenlik ve birini hükümdar yapma kullanımları kendi biçim ve kalıplarına bağlı tutulur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; genel yetki, yöneticilik ve özel sahiplikle en açıklayıcı üç sınır yayımlandı, üstünlük, azletme ve unvanla ilgili daha uzak adaylar elendi.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalı hükümdarın halk üzerindeki genel kamusal yönetimini kurar; komşu dal yönetici kişiden bağımsız olarak belirli bir hak veya eylem alanında verilen yetkiyi de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Hükümdar kişisi, ülkesi ve ilahi mutlak egemenlik de kapsama girer.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Belirli bir hak veya eylem için bir kişiye verilmiş yetki de kapsama girer.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da başkaları üzerinde geçerli yönetim ve yetki kullanmayı anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalı en üst kamusal hükümranlığa ve ülke ölçeğine yönelir; komşu dal ise atanabilen yöneticilik veya valilik makamını daha geniş biçimde kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Hükümdarlık, ülke ve mutlak egemenlik ölçeği bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir kişiyi yönetici olarak görevlendirme ve belirli yöneticilik makamı öne çıkar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki alan da bir topluluğu yönetme yetkisini ve bu yetkiyi taşıyan kişiyi kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalının nesnesi topluluk ve ülke, yetkisi ise kamusaldır; komşu dalın nesnesi belirli mal veya hak, yetkisi ise sahibin özel tasarrufudur.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Halk ve ülke üzerinde kamusal yönetim ve siyaset vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Belirli mal veya hak üzerinde kişisel aidiyet ve tasarruf vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da denetim, yetki ve hüküm kullanma düşüncesini paylaşır.

branches.source_phrase_ar: والاسم الملك لأن يده فيه قوية صحيحة (maqayis)؛ الملك لله المالك المليك (ayn)؛ الملكوت ملك الله وملكوت الله سلطانه (ayn)؛ الملكوت من الملك (sihah)؛ المملكة سلطان الملك في رعيته (ayn;tahdhib)؛ له ملكوت العراق وعزه وسلطانه وملكه (tahdhib)؛ الملك هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور (mufradat)؛ ملك القوم فلانا وأملكوه على أنفسهم أي صيروه ملكا (tahdhib)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, bu alanı halk üzerinde emir ve yasakla işleyen yönetim gücü etrafında toplar; hükümdar, hükümranlık, ülke ve ilahi mutlak egemenlik aynı kamusal yetki ekseninin farklı görünümleridir.

branches.what_is_ar: المَلِك والملوك؛ المُلك والسلطان والعز؛ ملك الناس وسياسة الرعية؛ المملكة؛ الملكوت وخاصة ملك الله
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس مجرد مِلْك اليد للمال؛ ولا مَلَك الملائكة

concept_gloss.applicability: Evlendirme, evlenme ve akdin gerçekleşmesi kullanımlarını ortak sözleşmesel çekirdekte toplar.

error_profile.preserves: Evlilik bağının akitle kurulması işlemini ve sonucunu korur.

concept_map.definition: İki kişi arasında evlilik bağını sözleşmeyle kurmak veya bu akdin gerçekleşmesidir. Kullanım, birini evlendirmeyi, evlilik akdine tanıklığı ve bir erkeğin bir kadınla evlenmesini kapsar.

facets.statement: Evlilik bağı, tarafları birbirine bağlayan bir akitle kurulur.
Bir kişi iki tarafın evlilik akdini kurarak onları evlendirir.
Evlilik akdinin yapıldığı tören veya ona tanıklık etme olayı adlandırılır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin iki taraf arasında evlilik akdini kurduğu bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Tarafın kendi evlenme eylemini ve akit törenini dışarıda bırakır.
error_profile.preserves: Akdi kuran dış katılımcının evlendirme eylemini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Taraflardan birinin evlilik bağına girdiği kalıplaşmış kullanımda uygundur.

error_profile.loses: Evlendiren kişinin eylemini ve akde tanıklık olayını dışarıda bırakır.
error_profile.preserves: Evlilik bağının taraf açısından kurulmasını korur.

error_profile.adds: Tek yanlı sahiplik ve nesneleştirme anlamı ekler.
error_profile.collision: Özel sahiplik dalıyla yanıltıcı biçimde karışır.
error_profile.loses: Karşılıklı evlilik akdini ve evlendirme olayını kaybeder.
error_profile.preserves: Bir ilişki kurma düşüncesini çok dolaylı biçimde korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kullanım mal sahipliği veya insanı köleleştirme değil, yalnız evlilik akdi ve evlenme bağlamıdır.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bütün örnekleri evlilik akdinin kurulması çevresinde toplar: birinin evlendirilmesi, bu akde tanıklık edilmesi ve erkeğin kadınla evlenmesi aynı sözleşmesel olayın farklı katılımcı görünümleridir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım evlilik akdiyle sınırlıdır; ad biçimindeki akit ve kadınla evlenmeyi bildiren kalıp ayrı yüzler olarak korunur, çıplak sahiplik anlamına genişletilmez.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; tam eşdeğer evlilik akdi, bedelin belirtilmediği özel akit ve cinsel birliktelik alanıyla sınırlar yayımlandı, akrabalık ve bekleme süresi gibi yalnız tematik adaylar elendi.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Verilen sınırlar bakımından iki dal aynı sözleşmesel evlilik olayını ifade eder ve olağan bağlamlarda birbirinin yerine kullanılabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da evlilik bağının akitle kurulmasını, evlenmeyi ve evlendirmeyi kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalı yalnız akdin kurulmasına ve evlenmeye yönelir; komşu dal evlilik akdinden cinsel birleşme ve bedenle ilgili örtmeceli anlamlara uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Evlilik bağını kuran akit ve evlendirme işlemi merkezde yer alır.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: evlilik akdi ve cinsel birliktelik alanı
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Cinsel birleşme ve beden bölgesi için örtmeceli kullanımlar da bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal evlilik ilişkisi ve bu ilişkiyi kuran akit bağlamında kesişir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal yalnız evlilik bedelinin adlandırılmadığı özel akit türünü belirtir; odak dalında böyle bir kurucu sınırlama yoktur.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Evlilik akdinin genel biçimidir ve bedel şartına bağlı değildir.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: genel ve bedelsiz belirtilen evlilik akdi
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Akdin kuruluşunda evlilik bedelinin belirtilmemesi özel koşuldur.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da taraflar arasında evlilik akdi kurulmasını anlatır.

branches.source_phrase_ar: كنا في إملاك فلان أي أملكناه امرأته (maqayis)؛ الإملاك التزويج قد أملكوه وملكوه أي زوجوه (ayn)؛ ملكت المرأة تزوجتها (sihah)؛ أملكنا فلانا فلانة إذا زوجناه إياها (sihah)؛ شهدنا إملاك فلان وملاكه وملاكه (tahdhib)؛ الملاك التزويج وأملكوه زوجوه (mufradat)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, bu dalı evlilik akdinin kurulması olarak ortaklaştırır; evlendiren kişi, evlenen kişi ve akde tanıklık edenler aynı sözleşmesel olayın farklı katılımcılarıdır.

branches.what_is_ar: عقد التزويج والإملاك؛ شهدنا إملاك فلان؛ ملك الرجل المرأة بمعنى تزوجها
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس ملك المال ولا استرقاق المملوك

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir düzenin varlığını ve düzgün işlemesini kendisine borçlu olduğu unsur için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Dayanılan unsur, ayakta kalma ve düzgün işleme ilişkisini birlikte korur.

concept_map.definition: Bir işin, düzenin veya bedenin ayakta kalmasını, düzgün işlemesini ve tamamlanmasını sağlayan temel dayanak unsurudur. Kalbin beden için bu işlevi görmesi verilen başlıca örnektir.

facets.statement: Bir unsur, daha büyük bir işin veya düzenin dayandığı ve onun düzgün işlemesini sağlayan temeldir.
Bu dayanak, işin doğruluğunu, sürekliliğini ve tamamlanmasını sağlayan belirleyici koşul olur.
Kalp, bedenin işleyişinin kendisine dayandığı temel unsur olarak gösterilir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir işin veya düzenin kendisine bağlı olduğu belirleyici unsur anlatıldığında uygundur.

error_profile.loses: İşin doğruluğu ve tamamlanması sonucunu açıkça belirtmez.
error_profile.preserves: Bağımlılık ve ayakta tutma işlevini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir işin onsuz yürümeyeceği temel unsur mecazlı ve doğal Türkçeyle anlatıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.adds: Beden parçası üzerinden güçlü bir mecaz ve örgütsel önem çağrışımı ekler.
error_profile.preserves: Temel destek ve vazgeçilmezlik ilişkisini korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal dayanak olan unsuru belirtir; nesnenin kendi iç sıkılığı veya sahiplik ilişkisi değildir.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir işin ayakta kalmasını ve düzgün işlemesini sağlayan temel dayanağı açıkça tanımlar; kalbin beden için örnek verilmesi bu genel bağımlılık ilişkisinin özel bir uygulamasıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnız dayanak bildiren belirtili kalıplarda geçerlidir; kökün çıplak biçimine genel bir temel veya öz anlamı yüklenmez.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; genel ayakta tutma, iç sağlamlık ve somut yapısal destekle en açıklayıcı sınırlar yayımlandı, öz, köken, yerleşme ve sınıflandırma adayları uzak kaldı.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalı belirli bir iş veya beden için kurucu dayanağı kalıplaşmış biçimde adlandırır; komşu dal ayakta tutan araçları geçim ve beden dâhil daha geniş alana yayar.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Anlam, dayanak bildiren belirli kalıplara bağlıdır ve bir işin doğruluğunu da içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: temel dayanak ve yaşamı sürdüren unsur
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Geçim, bedenin beslenmesi ve genel olarak varlığı sürdürme araçları da kapsanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir şeyin ayakta kalmasını ve işleyişini mümkün kılan temel unsuru anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalı ayakta kalmanın bağlı olduğu unsuru gösterir; komşu dal ise ayakta kalan şeyin kendi içindeki sağlamlık niteliğini gösterir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Ayakta kalmayı sağlayan belirli temel unsur adlandırılır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Nesnenin kendi parçaları arasındaki sıkılık ve tutarlılık adlandırılır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir şeyin bozulmadan veya çökmeksizin ayakta kalmasıyla ilgilidir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal somut taşıyıcı parçaları ve yerleşmeyi öne çıkarırken odak dalı bir işin doğruluğunu ve devamını sağlayan işlevsel temele uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Soyut işlerin veya bedenin işleyişine temel olan unsur da kapsanır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Kaburga ve yapı direği gibi somut taşıyıcı parçalar öne çıkar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da daha büyük bir bütünün üzerinde durduğu taşıyıcı unsuru anlatır.

branches.source_phrase_ar: ملاك الأمر ما يعتمد عليه (ayn)؛ القلب ملاك الجسد (ayn;sihah;mufradat)؛ هذا ملاك الأمر وملاكه أي صلاحه (tahdhib)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak açıklaması, bir işin kendisine dayandığı ve onun düzgün kalmasını sağlayan temel unsurdur; kalbin bedenle ilişkisi bu bağımlılık yapısını somutlaştırır.

branches.what_is_ar: ما يقوم به الأمر ويعتمد عليه؛ القلب ملاك الجسد
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس الملك للسلطان ولا ملك اليد

concept_gloss.applicability: Yol, vadi ve yerleşim kalıplarındaki orta, büyük veya bağlama göre sınır kesimini kapsar.

error_profile.preserves: Yer türünü, orta veya ana kesimi ve bağlama bağlı kapsam değişmesini korur.

concept_gloss.text: yolun veya yerin orta ya da ana kesimi

concept_map.definition: Yolun, vadinin veya yerleşimin bağlama göre orta, ana ya da büyük kesimidir; vadi kullanımında sınır da bu adlandırmaya katılır. Söyleyişe göre bu kesim izlenecek bir güzergâh veya uzak durulacak bir yer olabilir.

facets.statement: Bir yolun veya vadinin orta ya da ana kesimi belirli bir kalıpla adlandırılır.
Vadi için orta kesimin yanında sınır, yol için ise büyük bölüm açıklaması da verilir.
Aynı biçim bir yerleşimin orta veya büyük kesimi için de kullanılır.
Bağlama göre kişi bu ana kesimi izlemeye ya da ondan uzak durmaya yönlendirilir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yolun orta kesiminin izlenmesi veya boş bırakılması istendiğinde doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.loses: Yolun ana bölümü, vadinin sınırı ve yerleşimin merkezi kapsamlarını dışarıda bırakır.
error_profile.preserves: Yol ve orta kesim ilişkisini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Vadiye bağlı kullanımda kaynakların verdiği iki yer belirlemesini birlikte göstermek için uygundur.

error_profile.loses: Yol ve yerleşim kullanımlarını dışarıda bırakır.
error_profile.preserves: Vadi kullanımındaki orta ve sınır seçeneklerini korur.

error_profile.collision: İdari veya işlevsel merkez anlamıyla karışabilir.
error_profile.loses: Ana veya büyük kesim ile vadi sınırı seçeneklerini kaybeder.
error_profile.preserves: Orta yerde bulunma özelliğini korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Tanım yol ve vadi kalıplarıyla sınırlıdır; her nesnenin genel ortası anlamına genişletilemez.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yol ve vadi için orta kısmı açıkça verir, ancak vadi kullanımında sınır, yol kullanımında ise ana veya büyük bölüm de aktarılır. Bu yüzden dal yalnız geometrik orta nokta diye daraltılmamalı, yerin ortası, ana kesimi veya bağlama göre sınırı olarak tutulmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yolun ortası veya ana kesimi, vadinin ortası veya sınırı ve yerleşimin merkezi yalnız belgelenmiş biçim ve kalıplarda korunur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; yolun ana hattı, genel orta konum ve dönemeçle sınırlar yayımlandı, yolculuk, dağ yolu ve yer çıkışı gibi yalnız aynı alanda bulunan adaylar elendi.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalı belirli yol, vadi ve yerleşim kalıplarında orta ya da ana kesimi adlandırır; komşu dal yolun güzergâh ve açıklık niteliğini daha genel işler.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Vadi sınırı ve yerleşimin merkezi gibi kalıba bağlı kullanımlar da vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Yolun doğrultusu, açıklığı veya izlenmesi gereken güzergâhı daha geniş biçimde kapsanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da yolun ortası, ana kısmı ve izlenen doğrultusu alanında örtüşür.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal genel bir konumsal orta kavramıdır; odak dalı yalnız belirli yer kalıplarında orta, ana bölüm veya sınır olarak sözlüksel biçimde sınırlanmıştır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yol, vadi ve yerleşimle sınırlı ana kesim ve sınır kullanımları bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: yerin ana kesimi ve genel orta konum
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Her tür nesne, topluluk veya sıralı yapıdaki iki uç arasındaki orta konum kapsanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir bütünün uçları arasında bulunan orta bölgeyi gösterebilir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalı bölümün bütün içindeki konumunu veya büyüklüğünü gösterir; komşu dal ise yolun biçim değiştirerek kıvrıldığı geçiş noktasını gösterir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Yolun veya vadinin orta, ana ya da sınır kesimi belirtilir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Dağ veya vadide yolun kıvrıldığı geçit ve dönemeç belirtilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal yol ve vadi içindeki belirli bir yer bölümünü adlandırır.

concept_map.definition: Su, yolcunun veya bir topluluğun işini denetim altında tutmasını, konaklamasını ve geçimini sürdürmesini sağlayan temel kaynaktır. Suyun bulunmaması bu yeterliğin yokluğu, çok sayıda su kaynağı ise güçlü yaşam imkânı olarak anlatılır.

facets.statement: Su, yolcunun veya topluluğun işlerini yürütebilmesini sağlayan temel kaynaktır.

Suyun yokluğu çaresizlik, çok sayıda su kaynağı ise geniş yaşam imkânı olarak ifade edilir.

concept_map.definition: İlahi buyruğu veya haberi ileten haberci varlığın adıdır. Dal ayrıca kaynakların bu adı, haber götürme ve elçilik anlamıyla ilişkili daha eski biçimlerden açıklayan etimolojik kaydını kapsar.

facets.statement: Ad, ilahi haber veya buyruk ileten haberci varlığı belirtir.
Kaynaklar adın ses ve harf düzeni değişmiş daha eski biçimlerini aktarır.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal sözlükte kaydedilen varlık adını ve kaynakların etimolojik açıklamasını verir; güç, sahiplik veya egemenlik anlamı vermez.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, ilahi haberci varlığın tekil adını ve çoğul sınıfını doğrudan tanımlar; ayrıca adı haber götürme ve elçilik anlamıyla ilişkilendirilen daha eski biçimlerden açıklar. Dal, mevcut zarf içinde bu sözlük biçimi ve etimolojik açıklama olarak tutulabilir; güç, özel sahiplik ya da kamusal egemenlik anlamı sayılmamalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam çözümlenmemiştir; hiçbir çıplak kök anlamı varsayılmaz ve kavram yalnız kaynakta açıklanan ad ile etimolojik tartışma düzeyinde tutulur.

text.arabic_uthmani: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِۦٓ ۗ أَفَتَتَّخِذُونَهُۥ وَذُرِّيَّتَهُۥٓ أَوْلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِى وَهُمْ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّۢ ۚ بِئْسَ لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ بَدَلًۭا

baseline.text: Hani meleklere, Âdem'e secde edin, demiştik; İblis dışında hepsi secde etmişti. O cinlerdendi ve Rabbinin buyruğundan çıktı. Şimdi onu ve soyunu, size düşman oldukları halde, benim yerime dostlar mı ediniyorsunuz? Haksızlık edenler için ne kötü bir değişim!

findings.text: İblis'i ve soyunu dost edinmek, Rabbin buyruğundan ilk çıkışı kendi koruma düzeninde yeniden üretmektir.
İblis'in buyruktan çıkışı, toplu itaatin içinde gizlenen istisnayı açığa çıkarıp onun gerçek yönelimini görünür kılar.

activation_trace.role: Concealment supplies the covered inside-position from which the breach begins.
A ripe fruit exiting its peel gives fisq a material crossing-out function.
Binding command supplies the normative boundary crossed by that exit.
Repair, nurture, and completion make the breached order formative rather than merely coercive.

changed_reading.after: Iblis ruptured outward from a command that held him within a lordly order of formation and completion.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: كان من الجن ففسق عن أمر ربه
baseline_models.mechanism: The sequence moves from a concealed kind to an emergence out of lordly command: fisq is materially pictured as a fruit leaving its peel, so rebellion becomes a breach from a containing formative order rather than an isolated refusal.

activation_trace.role: Acquisition and adoption make the patronage a chosen installation.
Taking charge and managing an affair supplies the functional office assigned to the allies.
Otherness supplies the displacement of God by an alternative relation.
Explicit enmity makes the installed patron structurally opposed to its beneficiary.
Putting something in the wrong place diagnoses the patronage as relational misplacement.
One thing standing in another's place names the completed substitution.

changed_reading.after: The verse indicts the deliberate installation of an enemy and his line into God's place of intimate governance and support.
changed_reading.before: The verse forbids friendship with Iblis.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: أفتتخذونه وذريته أولياء من دوني وهم لكم عدو بئس للظالمين بدلا
baseline_models.mechanism: Taking is deliberate acquisition, wilaya is charge-bearing proximity, min duni installs an other in the relevant place, and badal names replacement. The question therefore exposes a governance substitution: an acknowledged enemy is installed in the near, managing position owed to God.

activation_trace.role: Minute particles and their spread make the offspring a distributed extension.
One thing following another supplies serial continuity to the patronage network.
Enmity identifies what persists across the distributed succession.
Adoption makes participation in that network an acquired relation, not mere exposure.

changed_reading.after: A single breach propagates through a dispersed succession that can be repeatedly adopted as near authority.
changed_reading.before: Iblis has descendants who may also be chosen as allies.

baseline_models.mechanism: Dhurriyya carries minute spreading while wilaya can proceed item after item. The singular rebel is thus extended into a dispersed and successive patronage network rather than remaining one remote antagonist.

activation_trace.role: Scattering grain or flour supplies the focus network's distributive image.
Serial following turns dispersion into successive patronage.
Dry, breakable vegetation supplies a perishable carrier for the network.
Winnowing and windborne flight supply the outward dispersal mechanism.
Moving air supplies the force that distributes the fragments.
Filiation supplies the contextual bridge from sons to the focus's offspring.
Adornment explains the immediate attraction of lineage-based continuity.
Endurance supplies the contrast that reveals the rival succession as nonlasting.

changed_reading.after: That succession behaves like attractive worldly growth: it propagates widely through lineage yet is structurally brittle and nonenduring.
changed_reading.before: The offspring form a distributed succession of hostile patrons.

context_deltas.mechanism: The brittle growth dispersed by wind gives physical dynamics to the focus's spreading offspring, while sons as worldly adornment contrasted with what endures gives that network a temporal profile: attractive succession that scatters rather than lasts.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies scattering matter, sons, adornment, and endurance; I map their sequence onto dhurriyya as a perishable propagation system. Alternatively, the two context ayat may only contrast worldly goods generally, without specifying the focus's hostile lineage.
structural_cues: 18:45 moves mixed growth into brittle wind-scattered matter; 18:46 places sons among worldly adornments and contrasts them with what remains.

activation_trace.role: Concealment supplies what the surrounding disclosure sequence overturns.
Acquisition identifies patronage as a deed entered into the audit.
Uncovering and appearance supply public exposure.
Driving and gathering everyone to one end supplies the audit assembly.
Binding inscription that establishes judgment supplies the durable ledger.
Exhaustive counting removes any small-scale refuge from the audit.
Presence and witnessed nearness make what was done immediately available.

changed_reading.after: The question anticipates public disclosure: even a hidden-origin alliance is an acquired, countable relation that will stand present in the ledger.
changed_reading.before: The question challenges a concealed enemy alliance in the present.

context_deltas.mechanism: The concealed origin and acquired alliance of the focus are set inside an exposure-and-accounting sequence: all are gathered, the record binds every scale of action, and deeds become present. Patronage choice becomes an auditable act that cannot remain under the cover associated with jinn.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies concealment, exposure, gathering, inscription, counting, and presence; I treat chosen patronage as one of the deeds made present. Alternatively, the audit sequence may frame all action without specially foregrounding alliance.
structural_cues: 18:47 exposes the earth and gathers all; 18:49 records small and large acts and presents what was done.

activation_trace.role: Adoption supplies the shared installation operator in the focus question.
Taking charge supplies the office humans assign to the hostile line.
The repeated adoption image makes God's refusal directly comparable to the human choice.
Departure from guidance classifies the rejected personnel by directional failure.
An arm-like helper who strengthens its principal defines the support function God rejects.

changed_reading.after: Humans delegate support and practical authority to misguiding agents in a role that God pointedly refuses to assign them.
changed_reading.before: Humans choose the wrong intimate or guardian.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated taking construction creates an asymmetry: humans install Iblis and his offspring as charge-bearing allies, while God explicitly did not take misleaders as an arm that strengthens Him. Wilaya is thereby revised from private affinity to delegated support and operational dependence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated taking verb and the arm-helper image; I infer that awliya here includes delegated operational support. A live alternative is that 18:51 only denies divine need and does not define every aspect of human wilaya.
structural_cues: 18:50 asks whether humans take the hostile line as awliya; 18:51 answers with God's refusal to take misleaders as an assisting arm.

activation_trace.role: Uninterrupted nearness supplies the protection claim put under test.
A raised call initiates the test of relational availability.
Partnership names the claimed reciprocal relation being tested.
Calling and verbal inclination direct the appeal toward the alleged partners.
Answering as returned speech supplies the response that fails to arrive.
Expanded distance reverses the focus's image of proximity.
A barrier between two parties fixes the failed relation spatially.

changed_reading.after: Their promised nearness is counterfeit: when invoked as partners, it produces no response and resolves into a separating barrier.
changed_reading.before: The chosen allies are near but hostile.

context_deltas.mechanism: The near relation promised by awliya is stress-tested by a call to claimed partners. They give no answering return, and the supposed closeness reverses into separation and an inescapable barrier.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies proximity, calling, nonresponse, distance, and barrier; I read the later scene as a functional test of the focus's chosen awliya. Alternatively, it may expose false partnership generally rather than only the Iblis relation.
structural_cues: 18:52 orders a call to the claimed partners, records nonresponse, and places a mawbiq between the two sides.

activation_trace.role: Emergence from a peel supplies the initiating outward breach.
Binding command supplies what the breach leaves.
Falling and becoming fixed supplies terminal arrival.
Turning away from a direction supplies the escape route that cannot be found.

changed_reading.after: Fisq opens a trajectory whose apparent freedom to exit terminates in a condition from which no redirection is available.
changed_reading.before: Fisq describes the past act of leaving command.

context_deltas.mechanism: A temporal reversal links Iblis's movement out from command to the criminals' fixed encounter with a destination from which no turning place exists. The initial breach is easy outward motion; its terminal condition is unredirectable arrival.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an exit image, fixed falling, and denied redirection; I supply the causal-temporal arrow from breach to no-exit destination. Alternatively, the two directional constructions may contrast rhetorically without encoding a single trajectory.
structural_cues: 18:50 marks movement out from command; 18:53 marks expected contact with the fire and the absence of any masrif away from it.

activation_trace.role: Adoption supplies the act that assigns the enemy a patronal status.
Putting something in the wrong place diagnoses the status assignment as misplacement.
Replacement supplies the exchange of proper and improper functions.
Stable correspondence to reality supplies the function the disputants try to dislodge.
Repeated adoption marks the same role-assigning operation applied to signs.
A manifest sign supplies the object whose evidentiary role is inverted.
Mockery supplies the false status imposed on signs and warnings.

changed_reading.after: The patron choice is one instance of a broader inversion technology that reclassifies enemies as protectors and signs as ridicule.
changed_reading.before: The bad exchange consists in choosing the wrong patron.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same acquisition operator that makes an enemy into a wali later makes signs and warnings into mockery. Together with zulm as misplacement and badal as substitution, this exposes a recurring operation: assigning a thing a role contrary to its true function.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated adoption plus two improper role assignments; I infer a common classificatory operation. Alternatively, ittikhadh may simply govern different objects without making the two errors one mechanism.
structural_cues: 18:56 uses ittakhadhu for converting signs and warnings into mockery after describing argument aimed against the stable truth.

activation_trace.role: Hiddenness supplies the external adversary's defining spatial quality.
Nearness supplies the route by which the hidden relation may become inwardly operative.
Abandoning and neglecting prior action supplies selective loss from awareness.
The heart supplies the interior site of the occlusive mechanism.
Protective covering supplies the layer that here blocks access.
Understanding supplies the capacity prevented by the covering.
Weight in the ear supplies a second material obstruction to reception.

changed_reading.after: The hidden enemy's nearness may be enacted internally as a covering system that edits memory, understanding, and hearing.
changed_reading.before: Iblis is a hidden external enemy whom people wrongly take as near.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's concealed adversary is followed by an internal apparatus of concealment: neglected prior action, covered hearts, blocked understanding, and weighted hearing. Chosen proximity can therefore be read as installing an occlusive filter inside perception, not only attaching to an external patron.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies external hiddenness, chosen nearness, and internal coverings; I infer that patronage can become a perceptual filter. A live alternative is that 18:57 describes an independently imposed judgment rather than an effect or expression of the alliance in 18:50.
structural_cues: 18:57 moves from reminder, turning away, and forgotten deeds to coverings over hearts and weight in ears.

activation_trace.role: Love, aid, and alliance supply the protection expected from the substitutes.
An other in God's place supplies the attempted alternative refuge.
Placement in the wrong location supplies the diagnosis carried into the closing example.
Substitution supplies the failed exchange of refuges.
A promise fixed to a time or place supplies the delayed deadline.
The repeated other-than relation directly tests the focus's alternative placement.
Flight to safety and rescue supply the refuge that cannot be found.
Falling into destruction supplies the realized failure of protection.
Repeated misplacement links the closing towns to the focus's wrong relational placement.
A second fixed appointment confirms that delay is scheduling rather than successful refuge.

changed_reading.after: It is a failed refuge contract: mercy may defer its exposure, but the substitute cannot shelter at the appointed reckoning.
changed_reading.before: Replacing God with hostile allies is a bad present choice.

context_deltas.mechanism: The proposed substitute patronage is tested as refuge under an appointed term. No place of safety exists apart from God, and the closing towns show misplacement reaching destruction at a fixed appointment; badal is therefore a refuge exchange whose failure may be delayed but is scheduled.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies substitute alliance, denied alternative refuge, wrongdoing, destruction, and appointments; I infer that the closing sequence operationalizes the focus's bad exchange. Alternatively, the towns may exemplify delayed judgment broadly without isolating patronage as their cause.
structural_cues: 18:58 combines a delayed appointment with no refuge apart from God; 18:59 joins wrongdoing, destruction, and another appointed time.

remaining_uncertainties: The command-as-containing-shell reading is an analogy activated by the sole fisq branch, not a claim that amr grammatically means a shell.
The distributed and contagious readings depend on materially distant branches and should remain exploratory where they exceed ordinary lineage and enmity.
The arrow from chosen hidden patronage to the covered heart and weighted ear is reader-supplied; 18:57 may instead describe an independent consequence or judgment.
strongest_changes: 18:51 revises awliya from generic friendship into delegated support: humans take misleaders as strengthening agents whom God refuses as an assisting arm.
18:52 and 18:58 expose counterfeit protection spatially: alleged nearness becomes nonresponse, barrier, and finally no refuge apart from God.
18:56 generalizes the bad exchange into role inversion: the same taking operation installs an enemy as protector and converts signs into mockery.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly turned abstract moral vocabulary into material and operational mechanisms: peel-breach, windborne succession, arm-like support, failed call-and-response, interior covering, and a refuge contract with an appointed failure.

activation_trace.role: Minute spreading supplies distributed carriers for the hostile relation.
Proximity without an interval supplies the contact condition for transmission.
A disease crossing from one bearer to another supplies an exploratory contagion model of enmity.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the hostile relation behaves like a transmissible pattern carried by dispersed successors and enabled by intimate proximity.
changed_reading.before: The enemy and his descendants are multiple hostile persons.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the disease-transfer branch under the focus root for enemy, not the ordinary enmity branch. It remains anchored by the exact عدو occurrence and gains coherence from ذرية as minute spread and ولاية as proximity; downstream prose should present it as a material analogy for propagated hostility, not as the lexical definition of عدو here.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: وذريته أولياء من دوني وهم لكم عدو

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Taking allies repeats the primordial exit from command.** `ر ب ب` B001 (“lordship, ownership, and authority”) governs the command from which Iblis departs. Humans then “take” that dissenter as protective authority, paralleling the youths’ people taking gods (18:15) and the rich man’s practical partnership (18:38–42). I infer that false alliance transmits an earlier refusal of rightful rule. The bad exchange is relational inheritance, not merely poor assistance.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:102 and 18:110 returned to false allies and servants, making this primordial refusal the closing relational danger.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Departure from command as self-exposure.** The accepted inventory for `ف س ق` retains only `ف س ق/B002`, the date emerging from its peel. The structural cue is a commanded collective (`فَسَجَدُوا`) followed by an exception, a statement of kind (`كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ`), and departure `عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِ`; the row in 18:48 and exhaustive book in 18:49 sharpen that separation. Exploratorily, I infer that leaving the containing order exposes what the apparent grouping had concealed. `فَفَسَقَ` reads as revelatory emergence through disobedience, not only movement away.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:51 denied the departing figure any creation-knowledge, and 18:52 showed his allied role failing under an actual call.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction launching a recalled primordial scene from the prior accounting frame
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) resumes the discourse and opens a remembered scene. It carries the reader from the preceding judgment and accounting frame into the primordial command story, so the later question about false guardianship is heard as evidence drawn from the beginning, not as an isolated warning.

topics.headline: resumptive launch from accounting to origin scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens by moving from end-time accounting into the remembered origin scene that explains the later choice.
topics.reason: QAC reads the conjunction as resumptive, and the boundary rows tie the previous justice-accounting scene to this remembered proof.

words.gloss_range: temporal recall marker governed by an implied remember, making the past scene function as present evidence
words.prose: {{ar:إِذْ}} ({{tr:idh}}) asks the audience to recall a past moment as live evidence. The Adam-prostration opening belongs to the familiar formula found elsewhere (2:34; 7:11; 17:61; 20:116), but here it narrows toward the question of whether humans will take the rebel and his line as allies.

topics.headline: past scene made evidentiary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the past Adam-Iblis scene is summoned as proof for the rebuke that follows.
topics.reason: The temporal adverb is governed by an implied recall command and introduces the Adam-prostration formula also seen in 2:34, 7:11, 17:61, and 20:116.

words.gloss_range: completed divine speech-act introducing the command; locally speech functions as authoritative command
words.prose: {{ar:قُلْنَا}} ({{tr:qulnā}}) is completed divine speech, but the quoted imperative makes the speech itself an act of command. The plural marker encodes the divine speaker inside the verb, and the recurring prostration formula makes this moment part of the known Adam-Iblis command scene.
words.root_gloss_range: broad saying and speaking field; local quoted imperative selects speech-as-command

topics.headline: completed divine speech as command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine saying is already an authoritative command, not mere narration.
topics.reason: The perfect first-person plural reports a completed divine speech-act, and its quoted imperative makes the utterance perform the obligation it states.

words.gloss_range: directional preposition marking the angels as recipients of the command
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) routes the divine command to its addressees. It marks the angels as the recipients of speech, distinct from the later {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) that marks Adam as the target of prostration.

topics.headline: command recipients marked before the target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this preposition marks who receives the command, before the next preposition marks where prostration is directed.
topics.reason: QAC and grammar rows identify this lām as the command-recipient marker attached to the angels, distinct from the later target lām before Adam.

words.gloss_range: definite angelic collective addressed by the command, genitive under the preceding preposition
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ}} ({{tr:al-malāʾikati}}) names the definite collective summoned by the command. The genitive form keeps the word under the recipient preposition, while the wider prostration-scene parallels (2:34; 7:11; 15:29; 17:61; 20:116; 38:72) make the later exception of Iblis a problem the ayah must explain, not a cancellation of the angelic address.
words.root_gloss_range: angelic agency with possible messenger or dominion associations; locally the lexical role is the angels as addressed collective

topics.headline: definite angelic collective under command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the commanded group is a definite angelic collective, while the Iblis exception will later require explanation rather than erase the collective command.
topics.reason: The local form is genitive under lām and definite plural; variant case pressure and root debates may be noted, but the local role remains the commanded angelic collective.

words.gloss_range: direct plural imperative to prostrate or submit in recognition; local command frame selects the prostration act
words.prose: {{ar:ٱسْجُدُوا۟}} ({{tr:usjudū}}) gives the command in bare imperative form. The plural ending addresses the whole angelic group, and the root range of prostration and submitted recognition is narrowed by the scene into a demanded act that the later perfect response will report as completed.
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes bodily prostration and submissive recognition; local imperative fixes the commanded act

topics.headline: direct plural imperative answered later
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the command as a direct plural imperative whose fulfillment is audibly and grammatically answered by the later perfect verb.
topics.reason: The Form I plural imperative selects bodily prostration or submitted recognition in this command frame and is answered by the perfect response at word 10.

words.gloss_range: directional preposition marking Adam as the target or direction of prostration
words.prose: This {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) does a different job from the earlier recipient marker. It points the commanded prostration toward Adam, keeping command-addressee and prostration-target grammatically distinct.

topics.headline: target of prostration separated from addressee
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar separates the angels as recipients of command from Adam as the directed target of prostration.
topics.reason: The second lām governs Adam and marks the prostration target, preventing collapse with the first recipient lām.

words.gloss_range: proper-name target of the commanded prostration in the Adam-Iblis scene
words.prose: {{ar:ءَادَمَ}} ({{tr:ādama}}) is the named target of the prostration command. The recurring Adam-scene formula keeps him stable across retellings (2:34; 7:11; 17:61; 20:116), while any earth-surface etymology remains secondary to his local role as the one toward whom the command is directed.

topics.headline: Adam as stable object of the formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Adam is the fixed named target in the recurring prostration formula, while earth-surface etymology remains only background pressure.
topics.reason: The proper noun is locally the target after lām in the formula recurring at 2:34, 7:11, 17:61, and 20:116; supplied root-image claims cannot override that role.

words.gloss_range: consequence conjunction marking immediate compliance after command
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) pivots from command to response with immediate consequence. The ayah does not linger between the imperative and obedience; it moves straight into the completed act.

topics.headline: immediate move from command to compliance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first consequence particle closes the gap between divine command and angelic response.
topics.reason: The particle is read as taʿqīb, making the completed prostration follow directly from the command.

words.gloss_range: completed plural prostration answering the imperative command
words.prose: {{ar:سَجَدُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:sajadū}}) reports the command as fulfilled. Its perfect plural form presents the angelic response as completed collective compliance, and its echo of the earlier imperative ties command and obedience tightly together before the exception appears.
words.root_gloss_range: prostration and submission-recognition field; local perfect reports the completed response

topics.headline: completed collective response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the commanded act has been fulfilled by the collective before the exception is introduced.
topics.reason: The perfect plural reports completed compliance and echoes the root of the imperative at word 6.

words.gloss_range: exception particle isolating Iblis from the collective compliance
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}) breaks the collective scene open. It isolates Iblis as the sole noncompliant figure, and that isolation creates the tension answered by the later statement that he was from the jinn.

topics.headline: single exception creates interpretive tension
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exception isolates Iblis from collective obedience and sets up the need for the jinn-classification clause.
topics.reason: The exception particle marks the first major pivot; any ambiguity about exception type is resolved locally by the following classification of Iblis as from the jinn.

words.gloss_range: proper-name exception from the prostration response, with refusal-scene associations
words.prose: {{ar:إِبْلِيسَ}} ({{tr:iblīsa}}) names the exception inside the prostration scene. The case keeps him grammatically connected to the collective response he refuses, while the name wider recurrence marks him as the figure repeatedly associated with prostration-refusal.

topics.headline: named exception tied to refusal scenes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Iblis is not a generic rebel here; his name is the recurring marker of prostration-refusal.
topics.reason: The accusative exception case keeps Iblis attached to this prostration scene, while foreign-name and Arabic-root readings remain interpretive apparatus.

words.gloss_range: perfect being-verb introducing an explanatory classification clause
words.prose: {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) interrupts the exception with explanation. It does not add another action by Iblis; it opens a classification clause, preparing the reader to hear his noncompliance in light of what he was.
words.root_gloss_range: being and becoming range; local clause classifies rather than narrates a new action

topics.headline: being-clause explains the anomaly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah pauses the action to classify Iblis, explaining why the exception is not simply another angelic response.
topics.reason: The perfect being-verb opens an explanatory clause, and the phrase uniquely resolves the anomaly in this retelling.

words.gloss_range: partitive or classificatory preposition marking origin or membership
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) gives the classification its grammar. It places Iblis from or among the jinn, making the explanatory clause a statement of membership rather than a vague comparison.

topics.headline: membership in the jinn class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Iblis is placed within a class, not merely described by a loose association.
topics.reason: The preposition functions partitive/classificatory in the predicate of the being-clause.

words.gloss_range: definite jinn-kind as the class to which Iblis belongs
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْجِنِّ}} ({{tr:al-jinni}}) names the known concealed class. The concealment field helps the label feel apt, and it also brushes against the surah garden vocabulary, but the local grammar selects jinn-kind as the class that explains Iblis exception.
words.root_gloss_range: concealment field yielding jinn, covering, garden, fetus, and related images; local sense is the concealed-being class

topics.headline: definite concealed class explains exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exception is explained through a definite hidden class, while garden-cover root associations remain secondary to the local classification.
topics.reason: The word is the genitive complement of min and names jinn-kind; the concealment root image supports the class label, but garden or madness derivatives are not the local sense.

words.gloss_range: causal and sequential conjunction linking the class statement to rebellion
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) mirrors the earlier consequence particle but with the opposite result. Where {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) moved command into compliance, this particle moves the Iblis classification into rupture from command.

topics.headline: classification leads into rupture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second consequence particle reversing the first: after obedience followed the command, rupture follows the Iblis classification.
topics.reason: The particle carries sequence and causality from the jinn classification into the act of fisq.

words.gloss_range: completed personal deviation or rupture away from the command
words.prose: {{ar:فَسَقَ}} ({{tr:fasaqa}}) makes the Iblis act a completed personal rupture. The root image of bursting out of containment survives as moral departure, and the following separation preposition keeps the movement directed away from a specific command rather than toward a vague state of badness.
words.root_gloss_range: bursting out, splitting, and moral departure field; local ʿan-phrase selects rebellion away from command

topics.headline: personal rupture away from command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices rebellion as a completed personal bursting-away from a specific command, not as vague disobedience.
topics.reason: The perfect Form I verb assigns the act to Iblis himself and takes the following ʿan-phrase as the point from which he departs; the root image is narrowed to moral rupture.

words.gloss_range: separation preposition marking the command as the point of departure
words.prose: {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) gives the rupture its direction. It marks separation from the command, so the Iblis fisq is anchored to a concrete divine order.

topics.headline: departure point marked by separation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices exactly what Iblis breaks away from: the command, not merely a general norm.
topics.reason: After fasaqa, the preposition marks directional separation from the command phrase.

words.gloss_range: specific command or authoritative affair in construct with his Lord
words.prose: {{ar:أَمْرِ}} ({{tr:amri}}) is singular and bound in construct, so the rupture is from a particular command. The root range of command and affair gives the word governance weight, while the following Lord-phrase specifies whose command has been violated.
words.root_gloss_range: command, ordering, governance, and affair range; local construct selects the violated command

topics.headline: specific command as governance-affair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what Iblis leaves is not generic instruction but the particular command bound to his Lord.
topics.reason: The construct singular binds the command to rabbihi; the command/affair semantic range remains relevant but is locally specified by the Lord relation.

words.gloss_range: his Lord, specifying the authority whose command Iblis violates
words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّهِ}} ({{tr:rabbihi}}) makes the violation relational. The suffix points back to Iblis, so the command he leaves is the command of his own Lord; the root nurture and sovereignty fields make the rebellion a break from rightful authority, not only from a rule.
words.root_gloss_range: rearing, sustaining, mastery, and sovereignty field; local suffix makes it the Lord relation of Iblis

topics.headline: his Lord makes rebellion relational
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Iblis rebels against his own Lord relation, not against an impersonal rule.
topics.reason: The suffix refers to Iblis and fuses the Lord relation into the command phrase; nurture/sovereignty root pressure is locally authority over the rebel.

words.gloss_range: interrogative plus consequential conjunction opening the direct rebuke
words.prose: {{ar:أَفَ}} ({{tr:a-fa}}) is the ayah confrontation pivot. The hamza turns the line into a rhetorical question, and its built-in consequence force carries the Iblis narrative into direct second-person accusation.

topics.headline: narrative turns into direct accusation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah suddenly turning from reported history into a second-person rebuke.
topics.reason: Interrogative hamza plus fa scopes the rhetorical question over the consequence of the narrative and triggers iltifāt into direct address.

words.gloss_range: ongoing second-person plural act of deliberately taking or adopting him
words.prose: {{ar:تَتَّخِذُونَهُۥ}} ({{tr:tattakhidhūnahu}}) names the deed under indictment. Its Form VIII shape makes the taking deliberate, the imperfect second-person plural confronts the audience, and the attached object keeps Iblis in view until the ally-complement names the role he is being taken as.
words.root_gloss_range: taking, seizing, receiving, and adopting range; Form VIII localizes deliberate adoption

topics.headline: deliberate adoption of Iblis as accused act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rebuke targets an ongoing deliberate adoption of Iblis, with him still visible as the direct object.
topics.reason: Form VIII supports deliberate taking/adopting, the imperfect second-person plural addresses the audience, and the suffix keeps Iblis as direct object while the complement comes later.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction adding the offspring of Iblis to the accused object phrase
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) widens the accused object phrase. It adds the offspring of Iblis to Iblis himself, so the false-guardian charge expands from one figure to a lineage.

topics.headline: offspring added to the object phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusation expands beyond Iblis alone to include his offspring.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the offspring with Iblis inside the object phrase of taking.

words.gloss_range: offspring of Iblis as a coordinated object of adoption
words.prose: {{ar:ذُرِّيَّتَهُۥٓ}} ({{tr:dhurriyyatahu}}) makes the false alliance generational. The accusative form joins the object of the adoption verb, and the suffix binds the offspring to Iblis, so the rebuke targets adoption of both the rebel and the propagated line associated with him.

topics.headline: possessed offspring extends the threat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the threat multiplying through the possessed offspring of Iblis rather than remaining a solitary enemy.
topics.reason: The accusative form joins the object of taking, and the suffix anchors the lineage to Iblis; variant and etymological rows sharpen propagation without changing the local object role.

words.gloss_range: plural protectors, allies, or guardians taken as the complement of adoption
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْلِيَآءَ}} ({{tr:awliyāʾa}}) supplies the role being assigned: protectors or authorities. The broken plural multiplies the role, and the nearness-authority root makes the charge sharper: the audience is taking the rebel line into a guardian relation that the next phrase places apart from the divine speaker.
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, succession, alliance, protection, and authority field; local exclusion phrase makes it false guardianship

topics.headline: enemy line taken as guardians
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contradiction: those descended from the rebel are assigned the role of near protectors and authorities.
topics.reason: The broken plural functions as object-complement of ittakhadha; the w-l-y nearness/authority range survives, but min dūnī restricts it into false guardianship apart from God.

words.gloss_range: preposition opening the apart-from-Me exclusion phrase
words.prose: {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) prevents the ally role from sounding like a neutral social role. It opens the compound exclusion phrase, turning false guardianship into a move away from the divine speaker.

topics.headline: guardian role opened as replacement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ally phrase does not close neutrally; it opens a substitution away from God.
topics.reason: The preposition begins the compound exclusion phrase min dūnī and keeps separation/substitution senses active.

words.gloss_range: apart from Me, marking exclusion and lower substitute authority
words.prose: {{ar:دُونِي}} ({{tr:dūnī}}) closes the exclusion phrase on the divine first person. The belowness and apartness field turns the false guardians into rival substitutes, and the suffix makes the accusation direct: the adoption happens apart from Me.
words.root_gloss_range: below, beneath, apart from, and exclusion field; local suffix makes the exclusion first-person divine

topics.headline: apart-from-Me as rival authority charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the standard false-protector formula becomes a first-person divine confrontation.
topics.reason: The first-person suffix makes the exclusion directly divine; d-w-n belowness/exclusion is local, while d-y-n dispute remains only secondary lexical pressure.

words.gloss_range: circumstantial conjunction introducing the enemy-status clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) turns the next clause into the circumstance of the accusation. The false guardians are not merely bad later; they are being adopted while already standing as enemies.

topics.headline: enemy status supplies the absurd circumstance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rebuke is sharpened by simultaneity: they are being taken as allies while they are already enemies.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces a ḥāl clause, making enmity the circumstance that exposes the absurdity of the adoption.

words.gloss_range: independent plural pronoun grouping Iblis and his offspring
words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) makes the enemy group stand visibly as subject. After suffixes attached to Iblis and his offspring, the independent plural gathers them together before the singular predicate names their shared enemy-status.

topics.headline: Iblis and offspring gathered as one group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from suffix possession to an explicit plural enemy group.
topics.reason: The independent plural pronoun gathers Iblis and his offspring as the subject of the nominal enemy clause.

words.gloss_range: to you or against you, an adversative dative directing enmity at the audience
words.prose: {{ar:لَكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) aims the enemy predicate at the audience. The lām is adversative here, so the same addressees who take Iblis and his offspring as allies are named as the targets of their hostility.

topics.headline: adversative dative aims enmity at the audience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the enmity is directed at the very people doing the adopting.
topics.reason: The lām plus second-person suffix marks the affected party of enmity and sustains the rebuke’s second-person address.

words.gloss_range: singular enemy predicate with collective force and durable hostile quality
words.prose: {{ar:عَدُوٌّۢ}} ({{tr:ʿaduwwun}}) is singular even though the preceding subject is plural. That grammar compresses Iblis and his offspring into one enemy type, turning the claimed ally role into its opposite: supposed protectors are in fact a durable adversary.
words.root_gloss_range: running, crossing bounds, hostility, and active enmity field; local predicate names durable adversarial status

topics.headline: plural false allies compressed into one enemy type
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammatical reversal: many supposed protectors are compressed into one durable enemy category.
topics.reason: The singular predicate applies to plural hum, supporting a unified adversarial category; rushing/hostility root pressure and recurrence around Iblis/Shaytan sharpen the standing opposition.

words.gloss_range: uninflected verb of dispraise giving categorical condemnation
words.prose: {{ar:بِئْسَ}} ({{tr:biʾsa}}) begins the closing verdict. Its frozen dispraise form turns the narrative and rebuke into categorical judgment, and the severity-wretchedness field makes the condemned exchange sound ruinously bad rather than merely mistaken.
words.root_gloss_range: severity, force, misery, and wretchedness field; local form is the frozen dispraise verb

topics.headline: frozen dispraise turns story into verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes by judging the exchange categorically, not merely by describing dislike.
topics.reason: The uninflected dispraise verb launches the final verdict; severity/misery root pressure is active in condemnation but locally serves the frozen judgment formula.

words.gloss_range: preposition specifying the affected class in the dispraise verdict
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) gives the verdict a target. It links the dispraise verb to the wrongdoers and specifies whose exchange is being condemned.

topics.headline: verdict assigned to the wrongdoers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dispraise is targeted: the wretched exchange belongs to the wrongdoers.
topics.reason: The preposition attaches the dispraise formula to the named class and specifies for whom the exchange is wretched.

words.gloss_range: definite active-participle class of wrongdoers, those misplacing trust and allegiance
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ}} ({{tr:al-ẓālimīna}}) names the condemned people by their ongoing agency. The root field of misplacement fits the accusation: they put trust and guardianship where it does not belong. Coming after 18:49, the label also shifts wrongdoing away from the Lord and onto the human exchange.
words.root_gloss_range: wronging, misplacing, darkening, and injustice field; local participle names the human exchangers

topics.headline: wrongdoers as the class that misplaces trust
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that wrongdoers are named by the act of misplaced guardianship, not by an external label.
topics.reason: The active participle names an agent-class, and the root field of misplacement/darkness is locally tied to taking the wrong guardians; the 18:49 contrast keeps divine non-wronging distinct from human wrongdoing.

words.gloss_range: accusative specification naming the condemned exchange or substitution
words.prose: {{ar:بَدَلًۭا}} ({{tr:badalan}}) is the final landing word. As accusative specification, it tells the reader what the dispraise condemns: the exchange itself. The substitution field makes the deal explicit: proper divine guardianship is traded for alliance with an enemy line.
words.root_gloss_range: replacement, substitution, exchange, alteration, and seeking replacement; local final word names the vile transaction

topics.headline: final word names the transaction itself
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah lands on the exchange itself: divine guardianship traded for enemy alliance.
topics.reason: The accusative tamyīz specifies the domain of dispraise, while the substitution root names the transaction; final position makes this the landing point of the ayah.
